paragraphs: We are a fully integrated biopharmaceutical company focused on developing innovative medicines for people impacted by central nervous system (CNS) conditions. We deliver scientific breakthroughs by identifying critical gaps in care and developing differentiated products with a focus on novel mechanisms of action, that have the potential to transform patient outcomes.

Our innovative CNS portfolio is anchored by three U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved commercial products: AUVELITY® for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD), SUNOSI® for the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) associated with obstructive sleep apnea or narcolepsy, and SYMBRAVO® for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults. Total revenues from our three commercial products totaled $638.5 million for 2025, representing 66% annual growth compared to 2024.

We are also advancing a deep pipeline of novel product candidates in early- to late-stage development addressing a broad range of serious neurological and psychiatric conditions. Our lead product candidate, AXS-05 (dextromethorphan and bupropion), is currently being developed for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease (AD) agitation and smoking cessation. In December 2025, the FDA accepted for filing the Company's supplemental NDA (sNDA) for AXS-05 for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease agitation. The application was granted Priority Review designation and a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of April 30, 2026. Solriamfetol is in Phase 3 clinical development for the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), MDD with EDS symptoms, binge eating disorder (BED), and excessive sleepiness associated with shift work disorder (SWD). We also have two novel, late-stage investigational products for the treatment of narcolepsy and fibromyalgia, as well as product candidates in earlier stages of development for the treatment of CNS disorders, including AXS-17 for the treatment of epilepsy.
Our goal is to efficiently develop and commercialize novel, differentiated therapies for the treatment of CNS disorders. The primary elements of our strategy to achieve this goal are the following:

• Pursue novel CNS indications with high unmet medical need. We believe that CNS disorders are significantly underserved therapeutic segments with currently limited treatment options. We are developing our product candidates for CNS indications where there exist significant unmet medical needs, or that have no or few FDA‑approved pharmacological treatments. CNS disorders are often disabling, difficult to treat, and associated with significant comorbidities. By focusing on areas of unmet medical need, we aim to develop products that have the potential to change current medical practice, and that are highly relevant to patients, physicians, and regulatory bodies. Many of these indications have significant patient populations, which, when combined with the limitations of current treatments, should provide us with attractive commercial opportunities.

• Develop products with our proprietary medicinal chemistry and formulation technologies. Our proprietary medicinal chemistry and formulation technologies allow us to continue to design new and innovative medicines to treat CNS conditions. These technologies and capabilities include: (1) chiral chemistry and formulation to identify, isolate and stabilize chirally pure enantiomers, (2) metabolic inhibition as a novel drug delivery method to increase the bioavailability and prolong the half-life of target drug molecules, (3) the MoSEIC, or Molecular Solubility Enhanced Inclusion Complex, technology which is designed to substantially increase the solubility and speed the absorption of target drug molecules, and (4) proprietary chemical synthesis and analysis to produce target drug molecules.

• Develop products with differentiated profiles. We aim to develop products with novel mechanisms of action for the intended indications that may yield differentiated product profiles. For example, AXS-05 combines several mechanisms of action resulting in a unique pharmacological profile that may be relevant to the treatment of numerous CNS disorders. The MoSEIC technology is designed to improve the absorption of drug molecules after oral administration and is utilized in SYMBRAVO (AXS-07). We believe that products with clearly differentiated features will be attractive to patients and their physicians and will provide us with a competitive commercial advantage.

• Reduce clinical and regulatory risk, limit development costs, and accelerate time to market. Some of our product candidates incorporate chemical entities with long histories of clinical use and well characterized safety profiles. Use of well characterized molecules has allowed us to rapidly complete early clinical development of our product candidates and may reduce the risk of late-stage clinical failures due to unexpected toxicities. This strategy may allow us to seek FDA approval for some of our product candidates using the 505(b)(2) regulatory pathway. Section 505(b)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, or FDCA, permits an applicant to file a new drug application, or NDA, that relies, in part, on the FDA's prior findings of safety and efficacy in the approval of a similar drug, or on published literature. It therefore allows us to leverage previous preclinical and clinical experience with the active molecules in some of our product candidates and potentially forego conducting certain lengthy and costly preclinical studies, reduce clinical and regulatory risk, limit development costs, and accelerate our time to commercialization.

• Retain commercial rights in the United States, where appropriate, and selectively partner outside of the United States to maximize the value of our product candidates. We intend to commercialize our products and product candidates, if approved, in the United States through the establishment of our own focused, cost‑effective sales and marketing organization. For commercialization outside of the United States, we intend to selectively partner with third parties outside of the United States to maximize the value of our products and product candidates, if approved, without the substantial investment required to develop independent sales forces in those geographies. We continue to evaluate strategic options for the commercialization of our other product candidates.

AUVELITY (dextromethorphan and bupropion) was developed by the Company and approved by the FDA for the treatment of MDD in adults in August 2022. We launched AUVELITY in the U.S. in October 2022 as the first and only oral, N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist approved for MDD in adults and the only oral antidepressant with rapid-acting efficacy reflected in the FDA label. AUVELITY utilizes a proprietary formulation and dose of dextromethorphan and bupropion, and Axsome's metabolic inhibition technology, to modulate the delivery of the components. Approximately 21 million people in the U.S. live with MDD.

SUNOSI (solriamfetol) is a novel, oral, dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (DNRI), trace amine-associated receptor 1 (TAAR1) agonist, and 5-HT1A agonist approved in the U.S. and Europe for the treatment of EDS in adult patients with obstructive sleep apnea or narcolepsy. We acquired the U.S. rights to SUNOSI from Jazz Pharmaceuticals plc, or Jazz, in May 2022, and the ex-U.S. rights (excluding certain Asian markets) from Jazz in November 2022. We have been commercializing SUNOSI since we completed these acquisitions. SK Biopharmaceuticals Co. Ltd., or SK, is the originator of SUNOSI and retains rights in 12 Asian markets, including China, Korea, and Japan. We refer to the acquisition of SUNOSI herein as the Acquisition. In February 2023, we entered into a licensing agreement, or the Pharmanovia License Agreement, with Atnahs Pharma UK Limited, or Pharmanovia, that granted to Pharmanovia the exclusive right to market SUNOSI in Europe and certain countries in the Middle East and North Africa, referred to as the Licensed Territory. Approximately 22 million adults and 185,000 people in the U.S. are affected by OSA and narcolepsy, respectively.

SYMBRAVO (MoSEICTM meloxicam-rizatriptan) is a novel, oral, rapidly absorbed, multi-mechanistic, selective COX-2 inhibitor and 5-HT1B/1D agonist that was developed by the Company and approved by the FDA in January 2025 for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults. We launched SYMBRAVO in the U.S. in June 2025. Approximately 39 million adults in the U.S. experience migraine.

Our extensive CNS development pipeline targets serious neurological and psychiatric conditions with significant unmet medical needs. We see significant long-term growth potential from our innovative early- to late-stage pipeline. We are leveraging our deep expertise and experience in neuroscience to maximize the potential of our approved products in additional CNS conditions, as well as advance our novel product candidates that we believe may, if successfully developed and approved, offer distinct advantages over currently available therapies.

AXS-05 (dextromethorphan-bupropion) is a novel, oral, investigational NMDA receptor antagonist, sigma-1 receptor agonist, aminoketone, and CYP2D6 inhibitor being developed for the treatment of CNS disorders. As used in this report, AXS-05 refers to, where applicable, AUVELITY as well as AXS-05 for the treatment of indications beyond MDD in adults. AXS-05 consists of a proprietary formulation and dose of dextromethorphan and bupropion and utilizes Axsome's metabolic inhibition technology. The dextromethorphan component of AXS-05 is an uncompetitive antagonist of the NMDA receptor, an ionotropic glutamate receptor, and a sigma-1 receptor agonist. Dextromethorphan is quickly eliminated from the body following administration due to extensive first pass metabolism, which results in low blood levels even at high doses. The bupropion component of AXS-05 serves to increase the bioavailability of dextromethorphan by inhibiting its metabolism and is a dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (DNRI). Based on its unique mechanism of action with multimodal activity, we believe that AXS-05 has potential therapeutic benefit for a variety of CNS disorders.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis contain forward-looking statements about our plans and expectations of what may happen in the future. You should read the following discussion and analysis in conjunction with "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data," and our consolidated financial statements beginning on page F-1 of this report. Forward-looking statements are based on a number of assumptions and estimates that are inherently subject to significant risks and uncertainties, and our results could differ materially from the results anticipated by our forward-looking statements as a result of many known or unknown factors, including, but not limited to, those factors discussed in "Item 1A. Risk Factors." See also the "Special Cautionary Notice Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" set forth at the beginning of this report.

We are a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the development and commercialization of innovative medicines for people impacted by central nervous system (CNS) conditions. We deliver scientific breakthroughs by identifying critical gaps in care and developing differentiated medicines with a focus on novel mechanisms of action that have the potential to transform patient outcomes.

Our broad commercial portfolio is comprised of AUVELITY, SUNOSI, and SYMBRAVO. AUVELITY is the first and only oral NMDA receptor antagonist approved by the FDA for the treatment of MDD in adults, which we are further developing in additional psychiatric conditions, including Alzheimer's disease agitation. SUNOSI is the first and only DNRI approved by the FDA for the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness associated with obstructive sleep apnea and narcolepsy, for which we also receive royalty revenue associated with sales in out-licensed territories. SYMBRAVO is approved by the FDA for the acute treatment of migraine in adults with or without aura, which we recently launched in the U.S. We are also advancing a pipeline of novel product candidates addressing a broad range of serious neurological and psychiatric conditions, including narcolepsy, fibromyalgia, and ADHD. Refer to Part I, Item 1. "Business" for a summary of our marketed products and clinical development programs.

Since our incorporation in January 2012, our operations to date have included organizing and staffing our company, business planning, raising capital, developing our compounds, engaging in other discovery and preclinical activities, the commercial launches of AUVELITY and SUNOSI, and preparatory activities for the launch of SYMBRAVO. Subsequent to our IPO, we financed our operations primarily through proceeds from sales of our common stock to equity investors and debt borrowings. For a further discussion, see the section entitled "Liquidity and Capital Resources" below.

Our ability to become profitable depends on our ability to generate revenue. We have recently begun commercial sales of AUVELITY and SUNOSI, and we launched SYMBRAVO, but we have limited experience with commercializing these, or any, products.

We have incurred significant operating and net losses since inception. We incurred net losses of $183.2 million and $287.2 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. Our accumulated deficit as of December 31, 2025 was $1,306.0 million, and we expect to incur significant expenses and continuing operating losses. We expect our expenses to increase in connection with our ongoing activities, as we continue the commercialization of our on-market products and the development and clinical trials of, and seek regulatory approval for, our current product candidates and any other product candidates that we develop or in-license and advance to clinical development. Further, we have incurred and will continue to incur additional costs associated with operating as a public company. Accordingly, we may need additional financing to support our continuing operations. We may seek to fund our operations through public or private equity, debt financings, or other sources. Adequate additional financing may not be available to us on acceptable terms, or at all. Our failure to raise capital as and when needed would have a negative impact on our financial condition and our ability to pursue our business strategy. We will need to generate significant revenue to achieve profitability, and we may never do so.
We generated total revenues of $638.5 million and $385.7 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

We expect that AUVELITY, SUNOSI, and SYMBRAVO revenues are likely to fluctuate based on demand quarter to quarter. We will not generate revenue from other products unless and until we successfully develop, obtain regulatory approval of, and commercialize one of our current or future product candidates. We have incurred significant operating losses since inception. If we fail to complete the development of our product candidates in a timely manner or obtain regulatory approval for them, our ability to generate future revenue from such product candidates, and our results of operations and financial position, would be materially and adversely affected. If we enter into licensing or collaboration arrangements, such agreements may or may not generate revenue in the future.

Additionally, in the fourth quarter of 2024, we recorded a milestone revenue of $0.5 million related to an achievement of a regulatory milestone in China for SUNOSI from SK. In the first quarter of 2023, we recorded license revenue of $65.7 million related to the Pharmanovia License Agreement (as defined below). See below for more detail.

In February 2023, we entered into the Pharmanovia License Agreement with Pharmanovia to commercialize and further develop SUNOSI in the Territory. Pharmanovia is a UK-based global life cycle management healthcare company that focuses on four core therapeutic areas – Oncology, Endocrinology, Neurology and Cardiovascular.

We received an upfront payment of €62.0 million ($65.7 million) during the first quarter of 2023 and are eligible to receive sales-based and other milestone payments totaling up to €94.5 million. We will receive a royalty percentage in the mid-twenties on net sales of the Licensed Products (as defined in the Pharmanovia License Agreement) in the Territory. We recognized royalty revenue of $4.7 million and $3.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, related to Pharmanovia's sales of SUNOSI.

Cost of revenue includes direct costs of formulating, manufacturing, and packaging drug product, overhead costs consisting of labor, customs, stock-based compensation, shipping, outside inventory management, royalty expense, and other miscellaneous operating costs. In the fourth quarter of 2024, we recorded a $2.5 million expense for the achievement of a sales-based milestone related to world-wide SUNOSI sales. In the first quarter of 2023, we recorded a $5.0 million license sharing expense related to the upfront license revenue received.

Research and development expenses primarily include preclinical studies, clinical trials, manufacturing costs, employee-related expenses including salaries, benefits, travel, and stock based compensation expense, contract services, including external research and development expenses incurred under arrangements with third parties, such as contract research organizations, or CROs, facilities costs, overhead costs, depreciation, and other related costs. In addition, research and development costs also include costs related to asset acquisitions involving clinical development programs that have not yet received regulatory approval.

Research and development activities are central to our business model. We have and will incur substantial costs beyond our present and planned clinical trials in order to file an NDA for any of our product candidates. It is difficult to determine with certainty the costs and duration of our current or future clinical trials and preclinical studies, or to what extent we will generate revenue from the commercialization and sale of AUVELITY, SUNOSI, and SYMBRAVO or our product candidates if we obtain regulatory approval. The duration, costs, and timing of clinical trials and development of our product candidates will depend on a variety of factors, including the uncertainties of future clinical trials and preclinical studies, uncertainties in clinical trial enrollment rate, and significant and changing government regulation. In addition, the probability of success for each product candidate will depend on numerous factors, including competition, manufacturing capability, and commercial viability. We will determine which programs to pursue and how much to fund each program in response to the scientific and clinical success of each product candidate, as well as an assessment of each product candidate's commercial potential.
本公司為一家完整整合的生技製藥公司，專注於開發創新藥物，以幫助受中樞神經系統（CNS）疾病影響的患者。我們透過識別照護中的關鍵缺口，並開發具有差異化產品的創新藥物，專注於新型作用機制，這些藥物有潛力改變患者的治療結果。
我們的創新 CNS 產品組合以三項美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准的商業產品為核心：AUVELITY® 用於治療重度抑鬱症（MDD），SUNOSI® 用於治療與阻塞性睡眠呼吸中止症或癲癇症相關的過度日間嗜睡（EDS），以及 SYMBRAVO® 用於成人急性治療偏頭痛（含或不含閃光）。我們這三項商業產品在 2025 年的總收入為 6.385 億美元，較 2,024 年成長 66%。

我們同時也在推進一項深具潛力的早期至晚期開發產品候選藥物，針對廣泛的嚴重神經系統與精神疾病。我們的領先產品候選藥物 AXS-05（右旋咳託明與布普品），目前正開發用於治療阿爾茨海默病（AD）的躁動與戒菸。2025 年 12 月，FDA 接受本公司提交的 AXS-05 補充新藥申請（sNDA）用於治療阿爾茨海默病躁動。此申請獲頒優先審查資格，並設定處方藥使用者費用法案（PDUFA）目標行動日期為 2026 年 4 月 30 日。Solriamfetol 正處於第三期臨牀開發階段，用於治療注意力不足過動症（ADHD）、伴隨 EDS 症狀的重度抑鬱症（MDD）、暴食症（BED）以及與輪班睡眠障礙（SWD）相關的過度嗜睡。我們同時還有兩項新型晚期開發的試驗性產品，用於治療癲癇症與纖維肌痛症，以及在較早階段開發的產品候選藥物，用於治療 CNS 疾病，包括 AXS-17 用於治療癲癇。
我們的目標是高效地開發與商業化用於治療 CNS 疾病的創新、差異化療法。我們實現此目標的主要策略如下：

• 追求具有高未滿足醫療需求的新型 CNS 應用。我們認為 CNS 疾病是嚴重被忽略的治療領域，目前治療選項有限。我們正在開發產品候選藥物，用於 CNS 應用領域，這些領域存在顯著的未滿足醫療需求，或目前沒有或僅有少數 FDA 核准的藥物治療。CNS 疾病通常會導致功能障礙，難以治療，並伴隨顯著的共病。透過專注於未滿足醫療需求的領域，我們旨在開發具有潛力改變現有醫療實踐的產品，這些產品對患者、醫生和監管機構而言都具有高度相關性。許多這些應用領域都有大量患者羣體，當與現有治療的限制結合時，應為我們帶來有吸引力的商業機會。

• 開發具有我們專有藥物化學與製劑技術的產品。我們的專有藥物化學與製劑技術使我們能夠持續設計新的創新藥物，用於治療 CNS 疾病。這些技術與能力包括：(1) 手性化學與製劑技術，用以識別、分離並穩定純手性對映體，(2) 代謝抑制作為一種新型藥物遞送方法，用以提高目標藥物分子的生物可用度並延長半衰期，(3) MoSEIC 技術，或分子溶解增強包含複合體技術，設計用以顯著提高目標藥物分子的溶解度並加速其吸收，以及 (4) 專有化學合成與分析技術，用以製造目標藥物分子。

• 開發具有差異化特徵的產品。我們旨在開發針對預期應用領域具有新型作用機制的產品，這些產品可能產生差異化的產品特徵。例如，AXS-05 結合多種作用機制，產生獨特的藥理特徵，可能對治療多種 CNS 疾病具有相關性。MoSEIC 技術設計用以提高藥物分子經口服後的吸收，並應用於 SYMBRAVO（AXS-07）。我們認為，具有明確差異化特徵的產品將對患者及其醫生具有吸引力，並為我們提供競爭性的商業優勢。

• 減少臨牀與監管風險，限制開發成本，並加速上市時間。我們的一些產品候選藥物 incorporates 化學結構具有長久臨牀使用歷史與已知安全資料的分子。使用已知分子使我們能夠快速完成產品候選藥物的早期臨牀開發，並可能減少因未預期毒性導致晚期臨牀失敗的風險。此策略可能使我們能透過 505(b)(2) 監管途徑尋求 FDA 核准部分產品候選藥物。《美國聯邦食品、藥物與化妝品法案》（FDCA）第 505(b)(2) 條款允許申請人提交新藥申請（NDA），部分依賴 FDA 對相似藥物核准時的先前安全與有效性評估結果，或公開文獻。因此，我們能利用部分產品候選藥物中活性分子的先前預臨牀與臨牀經驗，並可能避免進行某些耗時且成本高昂的預臨牀研究，減少臨牀與監管風險，限制開發成本，並加速我們的商業化時間。
• 維持於美國的商業權利，適當時機與美國以外的地區合作，以最大化我們產品候選品的價值。我們有意在美國透過建立自有且具成本效益的銷售與行銷組織，來商業化我們的產品與產品候選品（若獲批准）。於美國以外地區的商業化，我們有意選擇性與美國以外的第三方合作，以最大化我們的產品與產品候選品（若獲批准）的價值，而無需投入大量資金在那些地區建立獨立的銷售團隊。我們持續評估其他產品候選品商業化的戰略選項。

AUVELITY（右旋甲嗎啡與布普品）是由本公司開發，並於2022年8月獲FDA批准用於治療成人憂鬱症（MDD）。我們於2022年10月在美國推出AUVELITY，為首個且唯一口服的N-甲基-D-天門冬胺酸（NMDA）受體拮抗劑，用於治療成人憂鬱症，也是唯一口服抗抑鬱劑，其快速起效效果反映在FDA標籤中。AUVELITY利用專利配方與劑量的右旋甲嗎啡與布普品，以及Axsome的代謝抑制技術，來調節零組件的遞送。約有2100萬美國人患有憂鬱症。

SUNOSI（索裏阿美芬）是一種新型口服多巴胺與去甲腎上腺素再吸收抑制劑（DNRI）、痕跡胺關聯受體1（TAAR1）激動劑，以及5-HT1A激動劑，於美國與歐洲獲批准用於治療阻塞性睡眠呼吸中止症（OSA）或嗜睡症（narcolepsy）成人患者的日間嗜睡（EDS）。我們於2022年5月從Jazz Pharmaceuticals plc（簡稱Jazz）取得美國權利，並於2022年11月取得美國以外的權利（除外某些亞洲市場）。我們自完成這些收購後便開始商業化SUNOSI。SK Biopharmaceuticals Co. Ltd.（簡稱SK）為SUNOSI的發明者，並保留亞洲12個市場的權利，包括中國、韓國與日本。我們在此文中將收購SUNOSI稱為「收購」。2023年2月，我們與Atnahs Pharma UK Limited（簡稱Pharmanovia）簽訂授權協議（簡稱Pharmanovia授權協議），授權Pharmanovia在歐洲及中東與北非特定國家（簡稱授權地區）獨家市場SUNOSI。約有2200萬美國成人及185,000人患有OSA與嗜睡症。
SYMBRAVO（MoSEICTM 消炎痛-瑞西特普）是一種新型口服快速吸收、多機制、選擇性COX-2抑制劑與5-HT1B/1D激動劑，由本公司開發，並於2025年1月獲FDA批准用於治療成人偏頭痛（含或不含先兆）。我們於2025年6月在美國推出SYMBRAVO。約有3900萬美國成人經歷偏頭痛。
我們廣泛的神經系統（CNS）開發管線針對嚴重的神經系統與精神疾病，這些疾病具有顯著未滿足的醫療需求。我們認為從我們創新早期至晚期的管線中，有顯著的長期成長潛力。我們正利用我們深厚的神經科學專業與經驗，以最大化我們已核准產品在其他CNS疾病的潛力，同時推進我們的創新產品候選品，我們相信這些產品候選品若成功開發與核准，可能提供目前可用療法所無法提供的獨特優勢。

AXS-05（右旋甲嗎啡-布普品）是一種新型口服、正在研究中的NMDA受體拮抗劑、sigma-1受體激動劑、胺基酮與CYP2D6抑制劑，正在開發用於治療CNS疾病。在本報告中，AXS-05指的為適用時，AUVELITY以及AXS-05用於治療成人除憂鬱症（MDD）以外的適應症。AXS-05包含專利配方與劑量的右旋甲嗎啡與布普品，並利用Axsome的代謝抑制技術。AXS-05的右旋甲嗎啡成分為NMDA受體的非競爭性拮抗劑，為離子型穀氨酸受體，並為sigma-1受體激動劑。右旋甲嗎啡在給藥後會因廣泛的首過代謝而迅速從體內消除，即使在高劑量下，血液中的濃度仍低。AXS-05的布普品成分用以提高右旋甲嗎啡的生物利用度，透過抑制其代謝，並為多巴胺與去甲腎上腺素再吸收抑制劑（DNRI）。根據其獨特的作用機制與多模式活動，我們認為AXS-05對多種CNS疾病具有潛在的治療效益。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析包含有關我們計畫與預期未來可能發生事項的向前看陳述。請配合閱讀「第 8 項 財務資料與補充資料」，以及本報告自第 F-1 頁開始的合併財務資料。向前看陳述是基於許多假設與估計，這些假設與估計本身面臨顯著的風險與不確定性，因此我們的結果可能與向前看陳述預期的結果有重大差異，這是因為許多已知或未知的因素，包括但不限於「第 1A 項 風險因素」中討論的那些因素。請參閱本報告開頭所列的「向前看陳述特別警示」。
我們是一家專注於開發與商業化創新藥物的生物製藥公司，這些藥物可幫助受中樞神經系統（CNS）疾病影響的人羣。我們透過識別照護中的關鍵缺口，並開發具有差異化特性的藥物，來實現科學突破，重點在於具有潛力改變病患治療結果的新作用機制。

我們廣泛的商業產品組合包含 AUVELITY、SUNOSI 和 SYMBRAVO。AUVELITY 是美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准的第一且唯一口服 NMDA 受體拮抗劑，用於治療成人憂鬱症（MDD），我們正在進一步開發此藥物用於其他精神疾病，包括阿爾茨海默病的激動症狀。SUNOSI 是美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准的第一且唯一 DNRI，用於治療與阻塞性睡眠呼吸中止症及癲癇症相關的過度日間嗜睡，我們也因銷售於授權銷售地區而獲得版稅收入。SYMBRAVO 是美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准用於治療成人偏頭痛（有或無閃光）的急性藥物，我們最近已在美國上市。我們也在推進一系列新產品候選藥物，針對廣泛的嚴重神經系統與精神疾病，包括癲癇症、纖維肌痛症與 ADHD。請參閱第一部分，第 1 項「業務」，以獲得我們上市產品與臨牀開發計畫的總結。
自 2012 年 1 月公司設立以來，我們的運作包括組織與聘僱員工、業務規劃、籌集資金、開發我們的化合物、參與其他發現與臨牀前活動、AUVELITY 與 SUNOSI 的商業上市，以及 SYMBRAVO 上市前的準備工作。在我們首次公開發行（IPO）後，我們主要透過出售普通股給風險投資者以及借貸來資助運作。有關進一步討論，請參閱下文「流動性與資本資源」部分。
我們要成為盈利公司的能力，取決於我們產生收入的能力。我們最近開始銷售 AUVELITY 與 SUNOSI，並已推出 SYMBRAVO，但我們對這些產品或任何產品的商業化經驗有限。

自設立以來，我們已產生顯著的營運與淨虧損。我們在 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的淨虧損為 1.832 億美元，在 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度的淨虧損為 2.872 億美元。我們在 2025 年 12 月 31 日的累積虧損為 13.06 億美元，我們預期將產生顯著的費用並持續營運虧損。我們預期費用將因持續進行活動而增加，包括我們持續推廣現有上市產品，以及開發與臨牀試驗我們目前的產品候選藥物，並尋求其監管批准。此外，我們已產生並將繼續產生與作為上市公司運作相關的額外費用。因此，我們可能需要額外資金來支持持續運作。我們可能透過公開或私人家的股權、債務融資或其他來源來籌資。我們可能無法在合適的條件下或完全無法取得足夠的額外資金。我們未能在需要時籌資將對我們的財務狀況與追求業務策略的能力產生負面影響。我們需要產生顯著收入以實現盈利，而我們可能永遠無法做到。
我們在 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度產生總收入 6.385 億美元，在 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度產生總收入 3.857 億美元。

我們預期 AUVELITY、SUNOSI 和 SYMBRAVO 的收入將根據每季需求而波動。除非我們成功開發、獲得監管批准並商業化我們目前或未來的產品候選藥物，否則我們不會從其他產品產生收入。自設立以來，我們已產生顯著營運虧損。如果我們未能及時完成產品候選藥物的開發或獲得其監管批准，將會對我們從這些產品候選藥物產生未來收入的能力，以及我們的營運結果與財務狀況產生重大且不利的影響。如果我們與授權或合作安排簽訂協議，這些協議可能或可能不會在未來產生收入。
此外，於2024年第四季，本公司因SUNOSI在中國達成一項法規里程碑，而確認一筆里程碑收入，金額為50萬美元。於2023年第一季，本公司因Pharmanovia License Agreement（如下所定）而確認許可收入，金額為6,570萬美元。詳情請參見下文。
2023年2月，本公司與Pharmanovia簽訂Pharmanovia License Agreement，以於 Territory 內商業化並進一步開發SUNOSI。Pharmanovia為一間英國的全球生命週期管理醫療公司，專注於四大核心治療領域－腫瘤學、內分泌學、神經學及心血管學。

我們在2023年第一季收到一筆 upfront payment 約為 €62.0 million（$65.7 million），並有資格收到與銷售相關及其他里程碑付款，總計最高可達 €94.5 million。我們將根據 Territory 內 Licensed Products（如 Pharmanovia License Agreement 所定義）的淨銷售額，取得中位數二十幾% 的 royalty percentage。我們在2025年12月31日財務年度及2024年12月31日財務年度，分別認列 royalty revenue 約為 $4.7 million 及 $3.5 million，與 Pharmanovia 銷售 SUNOSI 有關。

Cost of revenue 包含直接成本，如製造、包裝藥品產品，以及 overhead 成本，包含勞務、關稅、股票基於報酬、運輸、外部存貨管理、royalty 費用及其他雜項營運成本。在2024年第四季，我們因全球 SUNOSI 銷售達成銷售里程碑，記錄 $2.5 million 的費用。在2023年第一季，我們因收到 upfront license revenue 而記錄 $5.0 million 的授權分享費用。
研究與開發費用主要包含臨牀前研究、臨牀試驗、製造成本、員工相關費用包括薪資、福利、差旅及股票薪酬費用、委外服務費用，包括與第三方簽訂的研發服務契約所產生的費用，例如合同研究組織（CROs），設施成本、間接費用、折舊及其他相關費用。此外，研究與開發費用亦包含與資產取得相關的費用，涉及尚未獲得法規核准的臨牀開發計畫。

研究與開發活動為本公司商業模式的核心。本公司將會產生遠高於目前及預期臨牀試驗的費用，以提出任何產品候選藥物的NDA。難以確定目前或未來臨牀試驗及臨牀前研究的費用與持續時間，以及本公司是否能從AUVELITY、SUNOSI、SYMBRAVO或產品候選藥物的商業化與銷售中產生收入，若本公司獲得法規核准。臨牀試驗及產品候選藥物開發的持續時間、費用及時程將取決於多種因素，包括未來臨牀試驗及臨牀前研究的不確定性、臨牀試驗入組率的不確定性，以及重大且不斷變化的政府法規。此外，每個產品候選藥物的成功機率將取決於多種因素，包括競爭、製造能力及商業可行性。本公司將根據每個產品候選藥物的科學及臨牀成功程度，以及對每個產品候選藥物商業潛力的評估，決定要推動哪些計畫及為每個計畫提供多少資金。
